I farm the way I have done for years: I start from what worked last year, then I shift a little if prices, labor, or weather push me. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too complicated, but after 55 years I know my land and I watch what the better growers around me do. I have 10.1 mu and I also have well water, so I will keep the safer land in wheat-maize because that brings grain every year, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. Family labor is not as full as before because some people work outside, so I will not spread myself too thin.

For wheat, I will put the stronger part of my money there because wheat is the first crop and if the stand is poor from the start, the whole year feels tight. I will use improved seed, rotary till once, put enough base fertilizer under it, and irrigate about three times if water is normal: one winter or freezing water if needed, one at jointing, one at filling. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose ears and grain. For maize after wheat, I will stay with hybrid seed because the yield is steadier and most neighbors do the same. I will keep fertilizer a bit heavy on nitrogen, give two irrigations in an ordinary year, and spray two times if worms and leaf disease show up. For cotton, I will only keep a small area because it takes more watching and picking. I will still plant it because I have done it many years and I do not like to put all my land into one road. On cotton I will not save too much on potash, because if cotton grows tall but does not hold bolls well, that money is gone anyway.
